free_tier.stated: Quoted from the programme page: 'It is $10,000 per project. All funding goes directly to the maintainers that are invited into the program. The funding is broken into tranches aligned to program schedules: $6,000 during program, $2,000 at 6 month check-in, and $2,000 at 12 month check-in.' The same page lists 'Cloud Credits: $10,000 in Azure credits. Eligible projects have potential to receive up to $150,000 in free Azure infrastructure credits from Microsoft for Startups.'

chaining: This is the only record that pairs cash with a cloud credit: USD 10,000 cash through GitHub Sponsors plus USD 10,000 of Azure credits, with a separate conditional route to as much as USD 150,000 of Azure infrastructure credit through Microsoft for Startups, so it composes with any Azure GPU quota the corpus records elsewhere.

quoted 'Session 4 runs late April with each project receiving $10,000, Copilot Pro, $100K of Azure Credits, and 3 weeks of security education' and 'an additional $5.5 million in Azure credits and funding' [this figure conflicts with the $10,000 Azure credits printed on the programme page; see notes]
reported: 'each project receives $10,000 USD via GitHub Sponsors', a 3-week sprint inside a 12-month engagement, and that 71 projects had taken part by that post
third-party confirmation of the USD 10,000 per project figure and the three-week programme shape

notes: The two first-party sources disagree on the cloud credit and the disagreement is the finding: the programme page prints 'Cloud Credits: $10,000 in Azure credits' with a conditional path to USD 150,000 through Microsoft for Startups, while a GitHub blog post describes session 4 as giving '$100K of Azure Credits'. I take the programme page as current and the blog as a launch-era figure, and the record states the page number; a reader should confirm with the programme before planning around either. Seventy-one projects had already passed through the programme by one of the posts, which is a large cohort for a fund this small and is the reason to rank it high: the odds are not Alpha-Omega odds. Two conditions do real work: the maintainer must sit in a GitHub Sponsors-supported region, and the project needs visible traction. A provider record for GitHub already exists in the corpus (github-actions, github-codespaces, github-student-developer); this is a separate programme with its own money and was absent from every GitHub record, so it is recorded as its own finding rather than as a duplicate.
